title: Letter Combinations (ç, ai, ei, an, am, en, em, ...)

sections.html: French spelling has many combinations where two or three letters make a single sound. Learn these and you will be able to read almost any French word correctly.

sections.heading: Soft and hard C and G
sections.html:
Spelling Sound Examples
c + a, o, u "k" café, code, culture
c + e, i, y "s" ce, ici, cycle
ç + a, o, u "s" ça, garçon, reçu
g + a, o, u hard "g" gare, gomme, aigu
g + e, i, y "zh" géant, girafe
gu + e, i hard "g" guitare, guerre
ge + a, o "zh" mangeons, Georges

sections.heading: Nasal vowels (the hardest and most "French" sounds)
sections.html:
A vowel followed by n or m (and then a consonant or end of word) becomes nasal: air goes through the nose and the n/m is not pronounced.

Spelling Sound Examples
an, am, en, em "ahn" (nasal, mouth open) France, chambre, enfant, temps
in, im, ain, aim, ein, un* "an" (nasal, like "bang" without the g) vin, simple, pain, faim, plein, un
on, om "ohn" (nasal, lips rounded) bon, nom, maison

*Many speakers today pronounce un the same as in.

Important: if the n/m is followed by a vowel, or is doubled, the vowel is not nasal: - bon (nasal) vs bonne (bo-nn, not nasal) - an (nasal) vs âne (ah-n, not nasal) - fin (nasal) vs fine (feen)

sections.heading: Consonant combinations
sections.html:
Spelling Sound Examples
ch "sh" chat, chocolat
gn "ny" (like "canyon") montagne, champagne
ph "f" photo, téléphone
qu "k" qui, quatre
th "t" thé, théâtre
ill (after a vowel) "y" fille, travailler, famille
s between two vowels "z" maison, rose
ss "s" poisson (fish) vs poison (poison)

exercises.answer: *ceci* – s, s; *coca* – k, k; *leçon* – s; *cinéma* – s.
*bonne* (double n followed by e → not nasal).

exercises.prompt: Explain the pronunciation difference between *poisson* and *poison*.
exercises.answer: *poisson* has **ss** = "s" sound (pwa-sohn); *poison* has a single **s** between vowels = "z" (pwa-zohn).

exercises.prompt: Read aloud and write the sound of the bold letters: **eau**, **ou**, **gn**, **ch**.
